description: Implement a single task from a Kotlin Multiplatform (Android + iOS app) `implementation_plan.md`-style task list — just the implementation and its tests. Detects the project layout at runtime (this catalog's `iru-setup-kmp-app` layout — `shared/` KMP module + `androidApp/` + XcodeGen-generated `iosApp/` — or the JetBrains wizard's older single `composeApp/` module, and whether the shared module uses the Android-KMP library plugin `com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library` or `androidTarget()` + `com.android.library`), whether UI is shared Compose Multiplatform (`ui: compose`) or native per platform (`ui: native` — Jetpack Compose in `androidApp`, SwiftUI in `iosApp`), and which module and source set the task belongs to (`commonMain` first, `androidMain`, `iosMain`, `androidApp`, or Swift in `iosApp`), then loads only the matching guidance from this skill's own `reference/` directory (always: mandatory rules — no platform API in `commonMain`, tests in the right source set, no `!!`, `@Throws` on Swift-facing throwing APIs, KDoc, no secrets, no edits to generated code — Kotlin code style with explicit API mode where enabled, and project structure with the default hierarchy template and `expect`/`actual` vs interface + DI; as needed: testing with `kotlin.test` + `runTest` + Turbine + fakes over mocks, shared logic — coroutines/`Dispatchers.IO`, Ktor with platform engines, kotlinx.serialization, kotlinx-datetime, SQLDelight/Room/DataStore, Koin or manual DI, multiplatform ViewModel — Compose Multiplatform with the `Res` class, navigation, previews and `MainViewController`, native UI over shared state, iOS interop as Swift sees it through the Objective-C header with SKIE/KMP-NativeCoroutines when present, KDoc/Dokka, security, and — for a task that adds or changes a screen, component or list — the catalog's UI contract mapped onto KMP: `Screen › Region › Component` decomposition reported back, stateless components over the shared view model's immutable state, `Lazy*` with `key`/`contentType` and SwiftUI `List`/lazy stacks for every collection, `runComposeUiTest` UI tests on the Android host (Robolectric) and the iOS simulator or Robolectric/`ImageRenderer` tests for native UI, capturing `.ui-screenshots/` across left-to-right/right-to-left × light/dark with an `--android`/`--ios` variant, and the accessibility check at the `.ui-quality.yml` level), re-checks the current code state, implements exactly what the task specifies, writes/updates tests in the right source set, compile-checks every target the touched source sets compile for with the Gradle wrapper (task names discovered via `./gradlew :<module>:tasks --all`; iOS targets only on macOS — never booting a simulator), regenerating the Xcode project with `xcodegen generate` when `iosApp/project.yml` changed, then — if the task didn't stop on a blocker — immediately checks off this task's own checkbox (and its sub-tasks') in `implementation_plan.md` with a "group validation pending" note, before handing back a short summary (layout/module/source sets detected, files touched, tests added/updated, compile-check result per target, any deliberate deviation from `reference/`, and any blocker). Does not capture a quality baseline, add license headers, update KDoc beyond the code it writes, run tests/coverage/detekt/ktlint/Lint/SwiftLint, or boot a simulator — those happen once per task group in `iru-kmp-code-one-task-group`, which invokes this skill once per task in a bucket (in parallel when the bucket allows it, through the `iru-isolated-skill-executor` agent). Invoke as `/iru-kmp-code-one-task <task description>`, passing the task's own text — including its exact `implementation_plan.md` checkbox line(s) — as the argument. The Kotlin Multiplatform counterpart of `iru-android-code-one-task`/`iru-swift-code-one-task`, for plan tasks tagged `kmp`.
